blocks.text: **I / you / he / she / it / we / they**

rows.example: **They** built the first aeroplane. · Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin, but **he** did it by mistake!

blocks.text: **me / you / him / her / it / us / them**

rows.example: Could you give **me** that equipment? · Could you give that equipment **to me**?

blocks.text: **my / your / his / her / its / our / their**

rows.use: To show who owns or has something

blocks.intro: Possessive determiners are always followed by a noun.

blocks.text: **Its** and **it's** do not mean the same thing.

blocks.correct: Here's the dog's water and here's **its** food. (= the dog's food)
blocks.incorrect: Here's the dog's water and here's **it's** food.

blocks.correct: **It's** the best camera I've ever had. (= It is …)
blocks.incorrect: **Its** the best camera I've ever had.

rows.use: To show who owns or has something

blocks.intro: Possessive pronouns are not followed by a noun.

blocks.text: There is no possessive pronoun for **it**.
**myself / yourself / himself / herself / itself / ourselves / yourselves / themselves**

rows.use: To describe actions where the subject and object are the same
rows.example: My computer turns **itself** off after half an hour.
Nobody helped me. I did it **myself**!

exercises.title: B · Object pronouns
exercises.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a word from the box.

items.prompt: Did you give **that book** back to Alicia? → Did you give ___ back to Alicia?
I told **Bill** that you don't eat meat. → I told ___ that you don't eat meat.
Why does she always give **our class** more tests than the other class? → Why does she always give ___ more tests than the other class?
They paid **Kate Winslet** a lot of money to be in this film. → They paid ___ a lot of money to be in this film.
I haven't seen **Rich and Andy** for ages. → I haven't seen ___ for ages.
Did you give an invitation to **Mr and Mrs Clark**? → Did you give an invitation to ___ ?
A TV channel has invited **my family** to take part in a game show! → A TV channel has invited ___ to take part in a game show!

exercises.title: E · Wrong reflexive
exercises.instruction: Each word in bold is in the wrong sentence. Write the correct reflexive pronoun.

This kitchen isn't going to clean **ourselves**, you know!
